newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall with eye set on Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall with eye set on Brazil.

text.p: Argentine bonds were trading lower at midday in a very volatile market with the attention almost exclusively centered on the Brazilian stock market, dealers said.
"Today is a complicated day," a dealer for a major national bank said. "Brazil is dominating the market. Few people are paying attention to the U.S. long bond."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down to $93.625/875 from Thursday's close of $94.125.
Dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was slightly down to 118.10/20 from 118.20/30.
Brazilian stocks took at midday a plunge of 8.17 percent with blue chip Telebras TEL p.SA shedding as much as 8.84 percent.

"Dealers are taking to the sidelines waiting for the landscape to clarifies," the dealer said. She added volume was normal and that there was heavy selling by the morning. "After that there was a slight recovery but I do not trust it very much."
Other dealers said the Argentine bond fall was also helped by a decline in the Dow Jones and the Bradies.
